issue.body:
Same class of problem as #3528, but in the sibling method.

```python
from starlette.datastructures import URL

print(URL('http://x/?a=1').replace_query_params(c=['d', 'e']))
# http://x/?c=%5B%27d%27%2C+%27e%27%5D  -- the repr of the list, one param

print(URL('http://x/').replace_query_params(c=('d', 'e')))
# http://x/?c=%28%27d%27%2C+%27e%27%29  -- same for tuples
```

Expected `http://x/?c=d&c=e` in both cases, matching repeated-key query encoding and the behavior of `include_query_params` after the fix for #3528.

The cause is the same one-liner pattern: `urlencode([(str(key), str(value)) ...])` stringifies the sequence instead of emitting one pair per item. Happy to send a PR mirroring the #3528 approach if that sounds right.

Env: starlette 1.6.0 (main @ d9ed5b0 range), Python 3.14.4, Linux.
issue.title: replace_query_params stringifies list and tuple values instead of expanding to repeated keys
